Decode: Character 3 = year letter: A=2003, B=2004, C=2005, D=2006, E=2007, F=2008, G=2009, H=2010, I=2011, J=2012 (sources say 'etc.' after J) / Character 2 = month letter: A=January through L=December. Decode: Characters 3-4 = last two digits of year / Character 5 = month letter (letter table only published as an image; not transcribed). Single source, era not stated. Olsen has other letter-coded styles (e.g. HTYL54759, 27191 BCKLU) whose letter tables are only in images, so not included.

Decode: Date printed on the data tag after the serial (or upper right corner of tag) as MM/YYYY: YYYY = year / MM = month. Not an encoded serial: the date is printed on the silver data tag. Decode: Character 1 = year letter: A=1984/2004, B=1985/2005, C=1986/2006, D=1987/2007, E=1988/2008, F=1989/2009, G=1990/2010, H=1991/2011, J=1992/2012, K=1993/2013, L=1994/2014, M=1995/2015, N=1996, P=1997, S=1998, T=1999, W=2000, X=2001, Y=2002, Z=2003 (I, O, Q, R, U, V not used; 20-year cycle, so A can also be 1964) / Character 2 = month letter: A=Jan, B=Feb, C=Mar, D=Apr, E=May, F=Jun, G=Jul, H=Aug, J=Sep, K=Oct, L=Nov, M=Dec (I skipped). Decode: The 2 digits after the leading letter = last two digits of year / Leading letter = month: A=Jan, B=Feb, C=Mar, D=Apr, E=May, F=Jun, G=Jul, H=Aug, J=Sep, K=Oct, L=Nov, M=Dec (I skipped). Decode: Characters 2-3 = last two digits of year; Character 1 = month letter: A=Jan, B=Feb, C=Mar, D=Apr, E=May, F=Jun, G=Jul, H=Aug, J=Sep, K=Oct, L=Nov, M=Dec (I skipped). Decode: nameplate production code: optional production company code (e.g. P1), then last two digits of year, then production week. Grundfos CR service manual 'Reading the pump nameplate' (A 12345678 P1 03 20). Grundfos safety notice https://www.grundfos.com/content/dam/global/page-assets/safety-warnings/Instructions-for-identifying-affected-grundfos-products.pdf confirms YYWW (1625 = week 25 2016). Decode: four-digit combined serial and date code: 2-digit year then 2-digit month. Armstrong circulator parts catalog 6010.201 'Serial number code' (June 2001 = 0106). Series 1050 with special materials carry a plain numeric serial instead

Decode: serial / Prod field = production week / 4-digit year / product identification. Armstrong VMS installation manual 47.84EU (European range); example from the manual. Keep the slashes when entering the serial

Decode: month letter (A=Jan, B=Feb, C=Mar ...) then the last two digits of the year written in reverse (32 = 2023, 41 = 2014). Source examples C32 = March 2023 and E41 = May 2014; it does not list all month letters or say whether I is skipped (only Sep-Dec affected). Parts Town notes the code is 2 or 3 characters depending on year and points to a per-product chart: https://www.partstown.com/cm/resource-center/guides/gd2/bell-gossett-serial-number-lookup. Era start unknown

Decode: four-digit code printed or ink-stamped on the valve body: first two digits = year, last two = week (YYWW). Source states this for most square aluminum-body gas control valves generally, with examples of week 37 1994 and week 19 1983. Resideo also moved its security/Home products to YYWW in June 2022 (older ones used a year letter + day of year, F = 2022): https://www.alarmgrid.com/blog/resideo-to-standardize-on-a-new-date-code-format-in-2022. Constructed example

Decode: four-digit date code on the back label: first two digits = year, last two = week. CPSC 2018 recall: 'date code from 1416 to 1536' = 16th week of 2014 through 36th week of 2015. Only confirmed for these thermostats

Decode: 10 digits: digit 1 = plant (1 = Helsinki), digits 2-3 = year, digits 4-5 = week, last five = unit.
